Salesforce AI Labs brings together AI-native businesses and software companies evolving toward agentic business models. Each has distinctive strengths, customers, and a focused go-to-market strategy. Our opportunity is to connect these capabilities into new ways for customers to operate, respond, and grow.

We are building a small team of hands-on technology builders who can turn that opportunity into working software and compelling business stories. You will connect products, models, agents, and data into demonstrable solutions—and help customers and executives understand their value.

This is a senior individual-contributor role combining software engineering, applied AI, solution architecture, and storytelling. You will move comfortably from a customer problem to code, from an API integration to a live demonstration, and from technical detail to an executive conversation.

Your mission

Build and demonstrate how capabilities across the Salesforce AI Labs portfolio can work together to deliver measurable customer outcomes faster.

You will show what customers can achieve with current capabilities, explore what becomes possible through new combinations, and make the path between the two clear.

What you will do

  • Build connected solutions. Create working prototypes, API integrations, and agent workflows spanning multiple products and enterprise systems.
  • Start with the business problem. Work with customers, portfolio leaders, and go-to-market teams to identify use cases where combining capabilities produces meaningful additional value.
  • Create compelling demonstrations. Develop reliable, repeatable experiences that make complex technology understandable and show a clear connection between customer needs, system actions, and business results.
  • Tell the story at every level. Present to executives, customers, developers, and sales teams, adapting the depth while preserving technical credibility.
  • Explore the next opportunity. Use rapid experimentation to test new agentic experiences and architectures. Clearly distinguish available capabilities, working prototypes, and future concepts.
  • Make the work reusable. Package reference architectures, integration components, demo environments, and playbooks that other teams can adopt.
  • Measure value and speed. Establish baselines and evaluate outcomes such as implementation time, process cycle time, cost to serve, service resolution, and customer experience.
  • Connect learning to product decisions. Surface integration gaps, customer demand, and technical constraints to product and engineering leaders, with evidence from what you build.



What you bring

  • A track record of personally building customer-facing software, integrations, or technical prototypes that solve real business problems.
  • Strong coding skills in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, or comparable languages, with the ability to build and debug across services and a usable demonstration interface.
  • Fluency in modern API architectures, including authentication, webhooks, event-driven integration, data contracts, and reliable execution across systems.
  • Practical experience building with models and tools from providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic, alongside relevant open-source agent frameworks and harnesses.
  • Understanding of tool calling, retrieval, orchestration, context management, evaluations, observability, and human approval within agent workflows.
  • Sound judgment about model limitations, reliability, latency, cost, data access, and the requirements for moving from prototype to customer deployment.
  • Strong storytelling and presentation skills, including the ability to deliver a live demonstration and explain its business significance.
  • The initiative to work through ambiguity, learn unfamiliar products quickly, and ship useful iterations with a small team.
  • The ability to turn a broad ambition into a testable use case with a credible path to customer value.



Experience that would be especially useful

  • Forward-deployed engineering, applied AI engineering, solutions engineering, or customer-facing solution architecture.
  • Building demonstrations or proofs of value involving multiple enterprise products.
  • Process intelligence, workflow automation, customer research, customer service, or digital experience platforms.
  • Creating reusable technical assets that support several customers or go-to-market teams.
  • Startup or founding-engineer experience with direct customer engagement.

These are proposed initial outcomes, to be calibrated to product access and team capacity:

  • First 30 days: Understand the portfolio, map integration opportunities, and select two high-value customer scenarios with business sponsors and measurable outcomes.
  • By 60 days: Deliver one working demonstration across multiple products, with a clear story, documented dependencies, and an initial evaluation of reliability and value.

日本の基幹産業である製造業界（ハイテク、自動車・モビリティ、重工・産業機械、素材・プロセス製造等）のエンタープライズ顧客を対象に、デリバリ（プロジェクト成功・価値実現）と、プロフェッショナルサービス、およびSignature Success PlanのGTM（Go-To-Market / サービス営業推進）との両面を包括的に統括・リードする部門責任者です。

ビジネス責任（Bookings、Revenue、Margin）を担うとともに、配下のピープルマネージャーを通じてチーム全体の成長、Equalityの浸透、エンゲージメント向上を牽引します。

株式会社セールスフォース・ジャパンは、Great Place To Work® Institute Japan（GPTW）が発表した2026年版「働きがいのある会社」女性ランキングにおいて第2位に初ランクイン、また大規模部門（1,000人以上）においても第3位に選出されました。

  • ウェルビーイング支援: 心身の健康を支援するウェルネス手当、社員サポートプログラム（EAP）など、持続可能なキャリアを支える包括的な福利厚生を提供しています。

Overview

We're looking for a dynamic, strategic, and outcomes-driven Public Sector Account Executive to drive Data Foundations growth across government agencies, departments, and public sector organisations. In this highly visible role, you will build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, identify new opportunities for engagement, and position Salesforce's industry-leading data management and analytics platform as a critical enabler of digital transformation across the public sector.

This is a quota-carrying role where you will act as the "CEO" of your territory, owning the strategy, engagement model, and execution plan across your assigned accounts. You will lead complex sales cycles in partnership with cross-functional teams and help government organisations address challenges related to data silos, data quality, fragmented reporting, and the need for trusted, unified data to drive better decisions and outcomes.

By bringing together strong account planning, consultative selling, and public sector insight, you will help agencies and departments modernise how they manage, govern, and activate data — enabling smarter policy decisions, improved service delivery, and accelerated mission outcomes.

This is not a typical software sales role. As a Public Sector Account Executive for Data Foundations, you will play a direct role in helping government organisations transform how they collect, connect, and trust their data. You will engage with decision-makers across agencies and departments to understand strategic data priorities, navigate procurement complexity, and align Data Foundations solutions to government-wide transformation agendas.

Success in this role requires a strong ability to build executive relationships, create demand, and drive long-term strategic engagement across a complex public sector environment.

What You'll Actually Be Doing
 

  • Territory Strategy: Develop and execute a comprehensive territory plan across government agencies and departments, identifying whitespace, prioritising target accounts, and building a clear engagement strategy aligned to agency data priorities and transformation goals.
  • Strategic Account Planning: Build detailed account plans that map stakeholders, business priorities, data environments, procurement pathways, and growth opportunities across assigned accounts.
  • Sales Leadership: Own and manage the end-to-end sales cycle from prospecting and qualification through to solutioning, negotiation, and close. Consistently meet and exceed sales targets through disciplined execution and value-based selling.
  • Executive Engagement: Build and nurture trusted relationships with senior government stakeholders, including department leaders, program owners, data and analytics leaders, IT executives, and procurement contacts. Establish yourself as a credible advisor who understands the public sector data landscape.
  • Drive New Engagement: Proactively create and expand engagement across agencies and departments by uncovering data challenges, initiating strategic conversations, and building momentum for Data Foundations solutions within both existing and new accounts.
  • Solution Selling: Identify complex data management, data quality, and analytics challenges within public sector organisations and position Data Foundations solutions to deliver measurable business and mission value, including improved decision-making, operational efficiency, and citizen service outcomes.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Lead and coordinate cross-functional support across Business Development, Solution Engineering, Customer Success, Marketing, Alliances, and leadership teams to drive account strategy and deliver a strong customer experience.
  • Government Market Insight: Maintain a strong understanding of the public sector landscape, including agency data priorities, procurement frameworks, policy considerations, funding cycles, and digital transformation trends.
  • Forecasting and CRM Discipline: Maintain accurate account plans, opportunity updates, pipeline visibility, and forecast hygiene in Salesforce CRM.


You're Our Person If...
 

  • Proven Enterprise Sales Success: Demonstrated success in enterprise software sales with a track record of meeting and exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.
  • Public Sector Experience: Experience selling into government agencies or departments, with a strong understanding of how public sector organisations operate, buy, and deliver transformation programs.
  • Data & Analytics Expertise: Familiarity with data management, data governance, analytics, or data platform solutions, and the ability to translate technical concepts into business value for government stakeholders.
  • Strategic Territory Management: Ability to build and execute territory and account strategies that create long-term pipeline and drive growth across a defined public sector portfolio.
  • Consultative Selling Skills: Strong ability to engage diverse stakeholders, uncover business needs, articulate value, and lead strategic, solution-based sales conversations.
  • Executive Presence: Confidence engaging senior leaders and navigating complex account environments with credibility, commercial acumen, and strong communication skills.
  • Cross-functional Leadership: Ability to orchestrate internal resources effectively and lead virtual teams to drive aligned execution and customer outcomes.
  • Resilience and Adaptability: Strong interpersonal skills, curiosity, and a growth mindset, with the ability to navigate long sales cycles, evolving priorities, and ambiguity.
  • Technology Affinity: Passion for digital transformation and an understanding of data platforms, analytics, data connectivity, and enterprise technology ecosystems. Familiarity with Salesforce Data Cloud or related solutions is advantageous.

We are hiring a Senior Director, Platform Product Management to build and lead a small, nimble product team for our platform. The vision is simple: a lean group that drives requirements, sets priorities, and evangelizes new platform capabilities across the org. Our Engineering, Development & Delivery (EDD) partners own all the engineering that brings those capabilities to life. Right now those capabilities exist as powerful but scattered building blocks. Your job is to shape them into a comprehensive platform. You will run continuous discovery with the teams who use the platform, translate their needs into a single sequenced roadmap, and work shoulder to shoulder with EDD engineers to ship.

This is a builder role. You need to be technical enough to earn trust with senior engineers (challenge scope, reason about architecture, cut through the noise) and strategic enough to rally the org around a clear plan without owning the engineers who execute it. Adoption is core to the job: advertising a service and waiting for uptake is not a strategy. You will own the “what’s in it for me” narrative and get partner teams to commit to real adoption.


What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Building the platform product function: Defining how the platform decides what to build, for whom, and in what order. Standing up the intake funnel and required functions to generate clarity and awareness of what is being delivered and when
  • Contributing to one platform roadmap: Consolidating initiatives spread across a dozen owners into a single, ruthlessly sequenced roadmap. You’ll contribute to making hard prioritization calls and defending them
  • Going deep with engineering: Sitting with senior engineers across hosting/compute, CI/CD and developer tooling, the AI control plane, data and telemetry, and real-time ML. Understanding the architecture well enough to challenge scope, unblock tradeoffs, and earn technical trust
  • Killing duplication: Maintaining the single view of who is building what. Merging overlapping efforts early
  • Driving adoption, not just availability: Owning the “what’s in it for me” narrative and pushing partner teams to commit to real adoption milestones
  • Running discovery: Interviewing platform use case owners continuously to keep the roadmap grounded in real demand, not assumptions
  • Communicating with clarity: Translating deep technical work into crisp narratives for executives and giving engineering a clear, honest read on priorities and progress
  • Mentoring PMs: Growing the platform product team as it scales; setting the bar for technical fluency and product craft

  • Experience in developer productivity or tooling: you’ve previously worked in environments where your primary mission was developer enablement

  • Intake and roadmap muscle: Proven track record building prioritization frameworks and driving one roadmap across many stakeholders and competing agendas
  • Adoption and go-to-market chops for internal or developer platforms: you have gotten teams to actually commit and migrate, not just express interest
  • Executive communication: You can hold a room with VPs and SVPs and make complex technical tradeoffs legible

descriptionHtml:

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The Experience

Salesforce is hiring a Senior Manager of Software Engineering to lead DNS Engineering, the team that owns the DDI (DNS, DHCP, IPAM) services infrastructure behind every Salesforce product. You'll lead a team of engineers responsible for authoritative and recursive DNS across Salesforce data centers and Hyperforce public cloud, self-service DNS and IPAM APIs, and DNS security, including DNSSEC and DDoS resilience. You'll set the multi-year strategy, own availability for this Tier-0 service, and lead the move to cloud-native, multi-provider DNS with automation and AI-assisted operations. The role suits a leader with 12+ years in software engineering, 5+ years leading teams, and deep experience with DNS and large-scale distributed systems.

Every customer request to Salesforce starts with a DNS lookup. The DNS Engineering team owns this layer for Salesforce: the authoritative and service-discovery DNS that sits in front of every Salesforce product, in our first-party data centers and across Hyperforce on the public cloud. We also own the DDI (DNS, DHCP, IPAM) platform and the self-service APIs that engineers and automated pipelines use to manage records, zones, and IP space every day.

The team's work spans large, mission-critical systems:

  • Authoritative and recursive DNS on BIND and dnsdist, running on fleets across many data centers and serving very high query volumes with strict latency and availability targets (3 & 4 nines).
  • Public cloud DNS on AWS Route 53 and GCP Cloud DNS, plus Kubernetes-native DNS automation (external-dns) for Hyperforce workloads
  • DDI platform and APIs: services that wrap commercial DDI platforms (such as Infoblox) so record and IPAM changes are safe, validated, and auditable
  • Security and resilience: DNSSEC, DDoS protection, hardening against dangling records and subdomain takeover, and multi-provider failover
  • Infrastructure as Code and automation: Puppet, Terraform, Spinnaker, and CI/CD pipelines with staggered, datacenter-by-datacenter rollouts, plus observability through Splunk, Grafana, and Argus
  • Third-Party DNS vendor relations: Our DNS infrastructure uses third-party DNS vendors to manage DNS zones on misc commercial enterprise DNS platforms.



As Senior Manager of Software Engineering for DNS Engineering, you'll lead the organization that keeps this layer fast, secure, and always available. You'll set its technical direction toward a cloud-native, highly automated, AI-assisted future. You'll lead tech leads, POs and senior engineers. You'll be accountable for availability and live-site health. And you'll partner with the platform, networking, security, and product teams that depend on DNS.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Set strategy and own delivery. Define the multi-year vision and roadmap for Salesforce DNS and DDI, and own execution from architecture through delivery to operational excellence across first-party and public-cloud environments.
  • Lead and grow the organization. Hire, develop, and keep a diverse, high-performing team of engineers. Set clear goals, manage performance, remove obstacles, and develop the next generation of technical leaders.
  • Own availability and trust. Treat DNS as Tier-0 infrastructure. Set availability, latency, and change-safety targets (SLOs), lead the incident and problem-management process, run blameless postmortems, and drive the fixes that keep the same incident from happening twice.
  • Modernize the platform. Lead the move toward cloud-native, multi-provider DNS on Hyperforce, including migrations, provider abstraction, Kubernetes integration, and retiring legacy systems, without disrupting customers.
  • Automate through AI and self-service. Grow self-service DNS and IPAM APIs, policy-as-code, and automated validation. Use AI-assisted development and agentic tooling to cut toil, catch risky changes before they ship, and speed up investigations.
  • Strengthen security posture. Champion DNSSEC, DDoS resilience, secure-by-default record management, protection against dangling records, and timely patching of third-party software, in partnership with Security.
  • Balance the portfolio. Weigh feature delivery, live-site work, operational load, and tech-debt paydown against each other, and make clear, data-driven tradeoffs that you can explain to leadership.
  • Partner across Salesforce. Represent DNS in architecture and planning forums. Turn the priorities of the platform, networking, Hyperforce, and product teams into a ranked roadmap with measurable outcomes, and resolve cross-team dependencies.
  • Communicate upward and outward. Report progress, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership, and act as the senior escalation point for DNS during critical incidents.



You're Our Person If...

  • 12+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years leading engineering teams
  • A record of building and scaling diverse, high-performing infrastructure or platform teams, and delivering complex, highly available production systems
  • Deep understanding of DNS and core internet protocols (DNS, DNSSEC, TCP/IP, HTTP, TLS, load balancing) and how they behave at scale
  • Experience owning Tier-0 or Tier-1 services in a 24x7x365, multi-datacenter environment, including on-call, incident management, and SLO-driven operations
  • Hands-on background in distributed systems, Linux, and backend development (Python or Go preferred), with sound judgment on system design, reliability, and operational risk
  • Experience with public cloud (AWS, GCP, and/or Azure), containers and orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker), and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Puppet, or similar)
  • Experience driving engineering productivity with AI-assisted development tools and automation
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders and peer organizations
  • A BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience



Even Better If...

  • Experience running authoritative and recursive DNS at internet scale (BIND, dnsdist, PowerDNS, Unbound, or similar) and with managed DNS services such as AWS Route 53
  • Experience operating DDI/IPAM platforms (such as Infoblox) and building self-service APIs on top of them
  • Led large migrations from data centers to the cloud, or from one provider to many, for critical network infrastructure
  • Background in DDoS mitigation, anycast, traffic engineering, or global traffic management
  • Experience building agentic or ML-driven tools for detecting, investigating, and fixing operational problems
  • Contributions to open source or to IETF/DNS community standards work

Salesforce is hiring Senior Forward Deployed Engineers — the Technical Builders, responsible for deciding that leads who design, build, and deploy the most complex agentic AI solutions directly inside enterprise customer environments. You’ll lead technical delivery on your team, mentor the next wave of engineers, and set the engineering standards that define how agentic AI gets deployed at scale. Partnering closely with a Deployment Strategist (Strategic Builder - a customer-facing advisor who shapes AI strategy and drives adoption), you’ll own outcomes end-to-end, from architecture decision to production. Your passion for well-crafted software that solves real problems will be supported by best-in-class AI tools and a team of talented builders around you.

The Senior Builder Experience

  • Technical Ownership: Partner with a Deployment Strategist to own customer outcomes end-to-end. You’re the senior technical authority in the room, ensuring deliverables meet the highest engineering standards, whether it was generated by an AI tool by a colleague or written by you directly.
  • AI-Supported Engineering: Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes are embedded in your daily workflow. The conventions and patterns you develop tend to propagate through the team because other Builders look to your work as reference.
  • Roadmap Influence: Your field experience routes directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps you hit and the edge cases you encounter in real life customer environments become the features they ship. Senior Forward Deployed Engineers are the most credible voice in agentic AI product evolution.
  • Continuous Innovation: You’re expected to stay at the forefront — piloting emerging AI tools, experimenting with new models and frameworks, and sharing what you learn with your team and customers.



What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Own end-to-end build and deployment of agentic AI solutions for Salesforce’s most strategic customers — from architecture decisions through production handoff.
  • Design and ship agentic systems on the Agentforce platform: agent logic, tool calls, multi-agent orchestration, deterministic guardrails, and the integration patterns that hold up in enterprise environments. Your reference implementations become the basis for how other Builders approach similar problems.
  • Own the data lifecycle: model design, processing pipelines, and data readiness for AI applications across Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer-specific platforms.
  • Resolve the technical blockers that other engineers can’t — data integration failures, model deployment issues, orchestration breakdowns, performance regressions. These problems are routed to you because of your track record of solving them.
  • Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes across engagements.
  • Develop proofs-of-concept and MVPs quickly, with the judgment to know which decisions can be deferred and which need to be right the first time.
  • Codify what you learn. The patterns, reusable assets, and internal frameworks that come out of your real customer work become the playbooks the rest of the org draws from.
  • Mentor other Engineers through code reviews, pair sessions, and shared work. Most of your influence on developing engineers happens inside the same codebases you’re building in.
  • Provide technical depth on at-risk or strategically critical deployments when senior engineering judgment is needed.
  • Surface field insights directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps and edge cases you encounter in real customer environments are some of the most valuable inputs to the Agentforce roadmap.
  • Partner with the Deployment Strategist on your team to translate complex customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.



You're Our Person If...

  • You have 6+ years of software engineering or technical delivery experience, with proven end-to-end ownership of scalable production systems in enterprise AI, cloud, or SaaS environments.
  • You have a degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • You’re an expert in at least one of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Apex, and conversant in the others.
  • You’ve integrated LLMs into production, used frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex, and applied prompt engineering and responsible AI practices in real customer contexts.
  • You have deep experience in data modeling, processing, and analytics, with demonstrable proficiency across platforms like Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, or Databricks.

  • You communicate clearly and credibly with engineering peers, customer architects, and executive stakeholders.

【セールスフォース・ジャパンの働きがいとダイバーシティ】


株式会社セールスフォース・ジャパンは、Great Place To Work® Institute Japan（GPTW）が発表した2026年版「働きがいのある会社」女性ランキングにおいて第2位に初ランクイン、また大規模部門（1,000人以上）においても第3位に選出されました。
弊社では「Equality（平等）」をコアバリューの一つとして掲げ、性別やライフステージに関わらず、すべての社員が能力を最大限に発揮できるインクルーシブな環境づくりを推進しています。社内コミュニティ「Salesforce Women’s Network（SWN）」をはじめとするネットワーキングやキャリア形成支援、メンターシップ制度も活発に稼働しています。

【働き方・ワークライフバランスの推進】


ハイブリッドワーク / リモートワーク制度: 業務内容やチームの取り決めに応じた在宅勤務（リモートワーク）とオフィス勤務の柔軟な組み合わせが可能です。
フレックスタイム制度: コアタイムにとらわれない柔軟なスケジュール調整が可能で、育児や介護、個人のプライベートな事情に応じた働き方を尊重しています。
充実した両立支援制度: 産前産後休暇・育児休業（女性の復職率は非常に高く、男性社員の育休取得実績も多数）、復職後の短時間勤務や看護・介護休暇など、ライフステージの変化に寄り添う各種サポートプログラムが整っています。
ウェルビーイング支援: 心身の健康を支援するウェルネス手当、社員サポートプログラム（EAP）など、持続可能なキャリアを支える包括的な福利厚生を提供しています。



The Experience

The Success Manager leverages deep business, industry and product knowledge to partner with customers and guide them to accelerate business value and return from their investment with Salesforce. In this role, the Success Manager will specialize in one or more line of businesses, a specific cloud or industry to speak the customer language and ensure customer value realization. They are aligned at key stakeholder level, building and fostering strong relationships to help customers progress on their digital journey. Success Managers are working directly with customers that can vary in their market segment, size, solution complexity and life cycle, depending on the customers needs. The ideal Success Manager, will possess both a Cloud specialization and industry skills that enables them to speak the customer language.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Leverage our Customer Success Methodology and partner with customers stakeholders to understand their goals, assess their capabilities and provide recommendations to help them accelerate achievement of their business and technology objectives
  • Develop an understanding and knowledge of customer's Salesforce implementation and evangelize the capabilities of Salesforce across all of our Clouds
  • Guide a customer on org strategy, governance and change management best practices based on customer needs
  • Can demonstrate hands-on Salesforce product knowledge by applying platform features and functions to customer business priorities and roadmap
  • Proactively identify risks to the customer achieving their stated business goals and work with the account team to build a risk mitigation plan
  • Produce and execute a comprehensive adoption path showing the current state, target future state with timeline, and an underlying enablement Plan
  • Deliver business value and innovation to a customer's business by understanding our customers' key business challenges and potential for growth
  • Build and foster executive-level relationships with the customer's IT and business executive leadership, sponsors and decision makers to solidify our partnership and commitment to the customer business and IT sponsors & stakeholders
  • Working collaboratively with the account team and Salesforce Execs, effectively network within accounts from the Executive-Level down, in order to help customers achieve their objectives
  • When appropriate, recommend additional Salesforce services and advisory experts needed to drive success
  • Proactively communicates technical product changes, degradations, outages, end of life and other relevant updates
  • Fluency in Japanese language skills (reading, writing, listening)



You're Our Person If...

  • 7+ years of proven experience in business consulting or solution sales
  • Demonstrated experience in the CRM space, including defining customer business challenges, driving sales process transformation, delivering solution proposals, and leading implementation and adoption
  • Strong consulting ability to understand customers' business objectives and help define and execute strategies and roadmaps that address their challenges
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and drive alignment among diverse stakeholders, including customers' Sales and IT teams and executive leadership
  • Proven ability to partner with internal and external stakeholders and take ownership of initiatives that deliver customer business value
  • Business-level or higher proficiency in Japanese (reading, writing, and speaking)

Even Better If...

  • In-depth knowledge in one or more line of businesses (LoB) - a specific cloud or industry
  • Strong consulting skills and proven results working as a Trusted Advisor to drive business value for customers
  • Ability to drive effective and influencing conversations at the C-level; facilitate difficult discussions and adept at handling objections
  • Strong knowledge of Salesforce product and platform features, capabilities, and best use is highly desired

About the Role Salesforce Belgium is looking for a curious and energetic Enterprise Account Executive with knowledge of technology, value-based solution selling, and a strong passion for the Manufacturing industry. This Business Unit sells the entire Salesforce platform—including Manufacturing Cloud—into a highly curated set of named enterprise manufacturing accounts (e.g., industrial goods, automotive, chemicals, high-tech manufacturing).

Think of yourself as the "General Manager" of your territory—mapping complex account strategies, aligning resources, and acting as the strategic extension of your customer. You will work closely with other product specialists known as co-primes to help map out the best digital transformation strategy for your customer. You will also have robust technical support from industry-aligned solutions architects and sales engineers.

You will collaborate with customers to evangelize solutions on the Salesforce Platform that bridge the gap between back-office ERPs and front-office customer experiences, helping them blaze new trails within their organizations. You will contribute to our business as a valued member of our Ohana.

  • Account Planning and Strategies: Establishes plans to achieve sales objectives by effectively identifying and qualifying complex, multi-site enterprise opportunities.

The Experience

Join an agile team with deep startup roots. We operate as a high-velocity ‘startup-within-Salesforce,’ following our recent acquisition. You’ll be managed by the same founders and engineers who built the original company, offering the autonomy of a small team backed by the global scale and trust of Salesforce.

We have successfully moved past the "0 to 1" phase. We have a product that works, customers who love it, and the backing of Salesforce. Now, we are entering the "1 to 100" phase: scaling our architecture to handle global demand, hardening our systems for enterprise-grade resilience, and integrating deeply with the Agentforce ecosystem. This is your chance to help lead that transition.


What You'll Actually Be Doing

As a Production Support Engineer (SMTS), you will be a senior technical member of staff within our embedded reliability team. You aren’t building the foundation alone—you’ll work alongside a group of engineers and product owners to ensure the Agentforce Operations platform is the most reliable AI-powered engine in the industry.


This is a role for an engineer who loves the "scaling" problem. You will focus on production excellence, performance tuning, and infrastructure automation. Because you are embedded in the product organization, you’ll have a seat at the table during design reviews, ensuring that as we add new agentic capabilities, they are built to scale from day one.


  • Scaling & Reliability: Own the reliability roadmap for major product areas, working to transition our systems from startup-speed architectures to highly-available, global-scale enterprise solutions.
  • Collaborative Leadership: Partner with PMTS-level engineers to refine our infrastructure strategy, contributing senior-level perspectives on system design, capacity planning, and bottleneck identification.
  • Infrastructure as Code: Maintain and evolve our automated environments, focusing on making our "infrastructure-as-plugins" model more robust and developer-friendly.
  • AI Operations (AIOps): Support the scaling of our AI/ML infrastructure, ensuring our models have the GPU resources and data pipelines required to deliver real-time supply chain insights.
  • Production Excellence: Lead the "1 to 100" hardening of our observability stack. You won’t just respond to incidents; you’ll build the tooling that prevents them and the telemetry that explains them.
  • Performance Engineering: Deep-dive into SQL optimization, API latency, and cross-service communication to ensure our data-intensive supply chain platform remains performant under heavy load.
  • AI-First Workflow: Lean into the future of engineering by using AI tools (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) to automate routine operational tasks and accelerate infrastructure delivery.

You're Our Person If...

  • 5+ years of experience in SRE, Production Engineering, or Backend Engineering with a heavy focus on operations and scale.
  • Proven Scaling Experience: You have previously helped take a product through a high-growth phase (the "1 to 100" journey), dealing with the technical debt and architectural shifts that come with it.
  • Coding Mastery: Ability to write and review production-level code in Golang, TypeScript, or Python—you view automation as a software engineering problem.
  • Technical Breadth: Strong proficiency in Kubernetes, Terraform/OpenTofu, and AWS/GCP/Azure.
  • Observability Expert: Demonstrated experience with properly instrumenting applications and platforms with SLO-based monitoring and alerting. 
  • Systems Expert: Deep understanding of distributed systems, including how to debug complex interactions between microservices, databases, and AI agents.
  • Low-Ego Collaboration: Experience working within a senior team of Principal engineers, capable of both leading specific initiatives and supporting the broader group’s technical vision.
  • AI Fluency: A demonstrated ability to use modern AI development tools to move faster and build more reliable systems.
  • Ownership Mentality. We are a senior team who operate with a high degree of autonomy. As a result, we’re looking for someone who can independently identify issues and own the solution all the way through final implementation.  

Even Better If...

  • M.S. in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
  • Database Specialist: Strong experience with PostgreSQL at scale (partitioning, indexing, query tuning).
  • Distributed Systems: Advanced knowledge of microservice orchestration and durability patterns, including hands-on experience with Temporal for workflow reliability and Istio service meshes for secure, observable service-to-service communication in high-growth SaaS environments.

The Migration Delivery Lead is an individual contributor who leads complex customer migration engagements from kickoff through successful go-live. You serve as the primary technical and strategic point of contact for your migration pod — building trust with customers, coordinating with our Global Delivery Center (GDC) engineering partners, and ensuring every engagement drives real, measurable value as customers move to modern cloud architectures.

This role sits at the intersection of customer relationship management and hands-on technical execution. You'll act as a trusted advisor who bridges a customer's legacy environment with their future-state platform — accelerating timelines through automated playbooks and AI-assisted tooling, while serving as a direct feedback channel to Product and Engineering on what's working (and what isn't) in the field.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Lead end-to-end customer migration engagements — owning technical delivery, project health, and successful go-live outcomes.

  • Build strong relationships with both business and technical stakeholders, translating complex migration challenges into clear, actionable decisions.
  • Develop and execute focused delivery plans that prioritize high-impact milestones and hold pod-level timelines to account.
  • Facilitate enablement and alignment sessions to ensure customer teams are prepared and confident for platform transitions.
  • Drive adoption of AI agents and automation toolkits to accelerate discovery, data mapping, and code conversion — reducing manual effort and compressing delivery timelines.
  • Collaborate closely with GDC partners, delegating repeatable technical tasks while maintaining full accountability for output quality.
  • Work in close alignment with Outbound Product Managers to stay current on product roadmaps and translate field insights into product improvements.
  • Identify underutilized platform capabilities and incorporate them into migration roadmaps to increase customer throughput and adoption.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert in at least one key domain: Marketing Cloud (Engagement/Intelligence), Data 360 (Data Cloud), Revenue Cloud (CPQ/Billing), or Tableau.
  • Apply AI literacy and prompt engineering skills to guide AI agents in data retrieval, migration health reporting, and task automation.



You're Our Person If...

  • 8+ years of experience in Professional Services, Customer Success, or Technical Consulting, with a strong focus on large-scale platform migrations.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive business value, facilitate technical discussions, and navigate complex stakeholder conversations.
  • Ability to translate complex technical architectures into business-friendly language and guide customers through data transformations.
  • Proven experience working with global or offshore delivery models (such as GDC) to accelerate project delivery.
  • Advanced knowledge of Salesforce core (Sales/Service Cloud) or specialized clouds (Marketing, Data, Revenue, or Tableau).
  • Familiarity with AI agents or automation tools applied to data mapping, sentiment analysis, or task automation.
  • Understanding of how target cloud platforms integrate with telephony systems, third-party data sources, and self-service portals.



Even Better If...

  • Certifications in relevant domains (e.g., Marketing Cloud Consultant, CPQ Specialist, Data Cloud Consultant, Tableau Desktop Specialist).
  • Prior experience as an individual contributor leading multi-million dollar transformation engagements.
  • Salesforce AI Associate or Agentblazer certifications.



What's in It for You
You'll join a team that is shaping how Salesforce customers adopt the next generation of cloud technology — with access to cutting-edge AI tools, a collaborative global delivery model, and a direct line to the Product teams building the platforms you work with. Unleash Your Potential

title: Senior Manager, Forecasting & Strategy
descriptionHtml:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Operations

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters
Salesforce is seeking a strategic, data-driven Senior Manager, Forecasting & Strategy to lead customer adoption forecasting and strategic planning across Customer Success. This role will develop forward-looking insights into how customers adopt, consume, and realize value from Salesforce products, enabling leadership to anticipate adoption trends, identify risks and opportunities, and make informed decisions that accelerate customer success.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and forecasting capabilities with strategic business acumen and a deep understanding of the customer lifecycle. They will translate complex customer, product usage, engagement, and operational data into actionable insights that help Customer Success leaders prioritize resources, improve adoption outcomes, and drive long-term customer value.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

Customer Adoption Forecasting & Analytics

  • Own and evolve customer adoption forecasting models that project product adoption, usage growth, Dollars used across customer segments, products, and portfolios.
  • Develop predictive models and leading indicators to forecast future adoption trajectories, identify customers at risk of stalled adoption, and surface opportunities to accelerate product usage.
  • Establish a consistent forecasting methodology, incorporating historical adoption patterns, customer health, implementation progress, success plans, and customer engagement signals.
  • Monitor forecast accuracy, identify variances between projected and actual adoption, and continuously refine forecasting assumptions, models, and methodologies.
  • Translate adoption data into clear, actionable insights on customer momentum, adoption barriers, risk, and expansion opportunities.


Customer Success Strategy & Planning

  • Partner with Customer Success leadership to develop strategic plans that improve adoption, accelerate time to value, and strengthen customer outcomes across the customer lifecycle.
  • Build data-driven frameworks to prioritize customer segments, identify adoption opportunities, and allocate Customer Success resources where they can have the greatest impact.
  • Develop scenario analyses and forward-looking projections to evaluate the potential impact of changes in customer engagement, product launches, enablement programs, and adoption initiatives.
  • Identify systemic adoption gaps and recommend scalable interventions, programs, and operating model improvements.
  • Connect customer adoption trends to broader business outcomes, including retention and growth potential.


Executive Insights & Business Performance

The Experience

Join our dynamic team at Salesforce and make a real impact with your code! We’re looking for passionate individuals who want to shape the future of our products and deliver exceptional experiences to our customers. Equally important is advanced prompt engineering — the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready. Come be a part of our innovative and collaborative environment, where your skills will thrive and your ideas will be valued. Apply now and let’s build something extraordinary together!

We embrace the hybrid model and celebrate the individual strengths of each team member while encouraging everyone on the team to grow into the best version of themselves. We believe that autonomous teams with the freedom to make decisions will empower individuals, products, companies, and customers to thrive.

About the Team:

Authentication Core decides how every user, admin, and integration signs in to Salesforce. We own login flows, session management, MFA, and the OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect and SAML endpoints that issue and validate credentials at global scale. We also own the defenses around them: binding sessions to devices (DBSC and Web Crypto) to prevent session hijacking, rolling out mTLS, enforcing PKCE and refresh-token rotation for connected apps, and retiring legacy login protocols. A mistake here is a security incident or a global outage, so we hold a high bar for correctness, security, and operations.

Your Impact:

Your work protects every Salesforce customer’s front door. You’ll ship security improvements to hundreds of millions of users without breaking the integrations enterprises depend on.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Architect, design, implement, test, and deliver highly scalable authentication and session services on Salesforce Core (Java), with strict availability and latency requirements
  • Build and evolve standards-based identity protocols, including OAuth 2.0/2.1, OpenID Connect, SAML 2.0, and newer ones such as PKCE, DPoP, mTLS-bound tokens (RFC 8705), token exchange, and Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)
  • Harden sessions and credentials against hijacking, replay, phishing, and credential stuffing, using token binding, refresh-token rotation, secure cookie design (SameSite, CHIPS), and step-up authentication
  • Threat-model new features, work with Product Security, and fix findings from penetration tests, bug bounty, and incident reviews
  • Roll out security enforcement safely for customers using feature flags, phased cohorts, telemetry-driven decisions, backward compatibility, and clear deprecation plans for legacy endpoints
  • Master our development process, culture, and code base, then improve it
  • Operate optimally in the hybrid engineering model where engineers are encouraged to be able to craft and complete the vital work to ensure quality in their own code as well as other engineers
  • Mentor others in development technologies, tools, processes, and secure-coding practices
  • Present your own designs to internal/external groups and review designs of others
  • Develop test strategies, design automation frameworks, and write unit/functional tests, including negative and abuse-case tests for authentication paths
  • Participate in the team’s on-call rotation to address sophisticated problems in real time, including authentication outages and security incidents, and keep services operational and highly available
  • Build and ship high-quality, production-grade software using modern engineering practices, with AI as a core part of your development workflow by pushing the boundaries of AI development tools to deliver secure, optimized, and high-quality code
  • Design and orchestrate complex systems where AI agents integrate seamlessly into human workflows, driving efficiency and innovation at scale
  • Contribute to building and maintaining the shared system context, an explicit repository of system designs, constraints, and standards that enables AI to operate accurately and reliably
  • Critically evaluate code (human or AI-generated) for correctness, quality, security, and performance, especially authentication, authorization, and cryptographic logic, where subtle mistakes become vulnerabilities



You're Our Person If...

  • A related technical degree required
  • 3+ years of professional software development experience (Senior Level: 5+ years, including ownership of production services)
  • Strong Java and object-oriented design skills; experience with large, multi-tenant codebases is a plus
  • Solid grasp of authentication and authorization basics: identity vs. access, session lifecycle, and token types (access, refresh, ID), with hands-on experience with at least one of OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, or SAML
  • Working knowledge of applied cryptography: symmetric vs. asymmetric encryption, hashing, HMAC, password hashing (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2), digital signatures, PKI and X.509 certificates, TLS and mTLS, JWT/JWS/JWE, and key management and rotation, plus the judgment to use vetted libraries rather than writing your own
  • Secure-coding fundamentals: OWASP Top 10, CSRF, XSS, session fixation, open redirects, injection, timing side channels, and safe handling of secrets and PII
  • Understanding of the browser security model: cookies and their attributes, same-origin policy, CORS, CSP, and security headers
  • Proven understanding of web technologies, such as JavaScript, HTML5, JSON, and HTTP
  • Validated understanding of database technologies such as SQL and relational database schema design
  • Experience in automated testing including unit and functional testing using Java, JUnit, and Selenium
  • A demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering: using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty, while using it responsibly with security-sensitive code (checking AI-generated cryptographic and authentication logic against specs, and never exposing secrets or customer data in prompts)
  • Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor) in development workflows
  • Advanced prompt engineering skills and the ability to write precise, structured prompts and cultivate the system context that makes AI outputs reliable, secure, and production-ready
  • Excellent interpersonal skills
  • Office-Flex: Work in-person three days per week; or 10 days per quarter for some engineering teams



Even Better If...

  • Experience building highly scalable web applications or identity infrastructure (identity providers, SSO, federation, token services)
  • Experience with MFA and passwordless authentication (WebAuthn/FIDO2, passkeys, TOTP)
  • Familiarity with identity RFCs and specifications (RFC 6749, 6750, 7519, 7636, 8705, 9449; OpenID Connect Core), or participation in the IETF OAuth Working Group or the OpenID Foundation
  • Experience with HSMs, cloud KMS, or secrets-management systems
  • Experience in regulated environments (FedRAMP, GovCloud, FIPS 140-3 cryptography)
  • A security track record, such as CVEs, bug bounty findings, security reviews, or incident response
  • Experience with Agile software development and test-driven development
  • Track record of being a top performer in current and past roles

As part of the Salesforce National Security (SNS) Infrastructure Security Team, the Incident Response Analyst will work on the 'front lines' of Salesforce environments supporting US Government agencies and departments performing national security functions.  The Infrastructure Security Team, protects our critical infrastructure and our customers' data from the latest information security threats. The team is responsible for 24x7x365 security monitoring, security operations, real-time analysis of security alert data,  and rapid incident response across SNS Cloud environments.

  • 2+ years experience in cybersecurity, engineering, and/or incident response roles.

  • Strong problem solving ability to determine solutions to encountered or anticipated challenges.
  • Strong technical understanding of the information security threat landscape (attack vectors and tools, best practices for securing systems and networks, etc.).
  • Experience with AWS Cloud, Splunk, Azure Sentinel, or ElasticStack, etc. preferred.



Even Better If...

  • Technical understanding of the information security threat landscape, to include attack vectors, tools, best practices for securing systems and networks, etc.
  • Technical understanding of TCP/IP network protocols and application layer protocols (e.g., HTTP, SMTP, DNS, etc.).
  • Familiarity with incident response and security operations within cloud environments.
  • Familiarity with Mac OSX, Microsoft Windows, and Linux/Unix system administration and security controls.
  • Technical understanding of AWS, Azure, or GCP administration and security controls.
  • Experience creating and managing event and metric dashboards with tools like Splunk, Kibana, Grafana, etc.
  • Experience with data query languages, such as SQL, SPL, GraphQL, etc.
  • Scripting language (i.e. Bash, Python, etc.) and workflow automation experience.
  • Operational experience monitoring devices such as network and host-based intrusion detection systems, web application firewalls, database security monitoring systems, firewalls/routers/switches, proxy servers, antivirus systems, file integrity monitoring tools, and operating system logs.
  • System forensics/investigation skills, including analyzing system artifacts (file system, memory, running processes, network connections) for indicators of infection/compromise.
  • Relevant information security certifications, such as CISSP, GCFR, GCIA, GCIH or other related certifications.

Developer Workspaces runs the computers Slack engineers write code on - and more and more, the ones AI agents write code on. Every week, hundreds of engineers build and test Slack in the remote development environments we run on AWS and Kubernetes. Now we're building the next layer: fast, isolated sandboxes where coding agents can run a dev toolchain, open pull requests, and shut down when they're done.


If most of Slack's code is going to be written by agents, it'll be written on infrastructure this team owns.


We're a small team with a lot of surface area. We're strong on backend engineering, and we need more depth in infrastructure and operations. That's this role. You'll own production systems early, carry the pager, and help decide how agents run safely at Slack.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Scale our AI sandbox fleet into something the whole company depends on - capacity planning, safe rollouts, image builds, and the alerts that tell us when it's breaking.
  • Harden the isolation between agents, sandboxes and the rest of Slack: network separation, egress controls, secrets handling, and patching.
  • Run and improve the remote dev environments our engineers use every day, from Terraform and machine images to the automation that pauses idle environments so they don't burn money.
  • Build observability we can make decisions with - SLOs, dashboards, and logs that land where we can find them.
  • Join our weekly on-call rotation once you've ramped up. Most pages are low urgency. When something does break, we fix it and then automate the fix.
  • Use AI agents heavily in your own work. You're building the platform they run on, so you should know what they need.

You're Our Person If...

  • You have 3+ years of experience building and operating production systems.
  • You come from infrastructure, SRE, DevOps or platform engineering, and you've been on call for something that mattered.
  • You know AWS well - EC2, networking, IAM - and you manage infrastructure as code with Terraform or something like it.
  • You write solid code in Go or Python. Everything we do ships as code, and your infrastructure instincts shape how you write it.
  • You use AI coding tools every day and have opinions about where they fall short.
  • You take ownership. When something breaks, you don't wait for someone to assign it to you.

Even Better If...

  • Content Development: Develop and maintain repeatable GTM assets, including sales plays, messaging frameworks, competitor-focused content, and demo libraries, aligned to launch and campaign rhythms.
  • Cross-Cloud Alignment: Act as the Data 360 subject matter expert across Salesforce clouds (Sales, Service, Marketing, Commerce, etc.) to ensure unified value messaging and solution positioning.
  • Pace and Adaptability: Thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, staying comfortable with ambiguity while maintaining clarity, precision, and executional excellence.

  • Experience: 3–5+ years in Product Marketing, Solution Engineering, Sales, or Go-To-Market roles within B2B SaaS or enterprise technology.
  • Product Knowledge: Working understanding of data platforms (CDP, data management, integration, or analytics) and enterprise AI, and how data powers AI outcomes.
  • Technical Fluency: Ability to translate technical capabilities into clear business value for varied audiences.
  • Collaboration: Proven ability to partner with Core Product Marketers, Product Managers, and cross-functional stakeholders to align launches, messaging, and roadmap priorities.
  • Sales Partnership: Experience working with Sales Leadership, Account Executives, and Sales Programs to turn GTM strategy into field-ready execution.
  • Enablement Expertise: Success developing sales plays, enablement programs, and training materials that drive adoption and measurable pipeline impact.
  • Communication: Strong presentation and storytelling skills, with the ability to deliver persuasive, executive-ready content.
  • Pricing Acumen: Familiarity with consumption-based pricing and skill in simplifying complex pricing into customer-centric value narratives.
  • Analytical Rigor: Data-driven mindset, using insights to inform GTM strategy, measure success, and refine programs.
  • Project Management: Organized and effective at managing multiple priorities and timelines.
  • Influence: Collaborative, with the ability to drive alignment across global and cross-functional teams.



Even Better If...

The Experience

Every service on a global, multi-cloud platform rests on one foundation: trust. The systems that issue certificates, establish workload and AI agent identity, and protect cryptographic keys let millions of services prove their identity to one another.


As an Architect, you define the strategy and technical direction for this foundation as the industry moves to shorter certificate lifetimes, fully automated lifecycle management, and post-quantum cryptography.


This is a hands-on architecture role for a distributed-systems leader with strong security depth. You design for continuous global availability, guide the evolution of our cryptography without disrupting dependent services, and implement working systems across multiple engineering teams. Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and key-management expertise are strong advantages, but deep distributed-systems and security judgment matter most.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Own the target architecture and multi-year strategy for certificate lifecycle, trust distribution, and cryptographic identity across workloads and AI agents, and lead execution through production.
  • Architect highly available, globally scalable trust infrastructure with measurable Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and fleet-wide automated certificate renewal capabilities.
  • Drive automation-first, cost-effective architecture focused on zero-touch lifecycle operations, zero-downtime migrations, and data-driven build-versus-buy decisions.
  • Establish architectural and security standards for the interfaces between the trust platform and dependent infrastructure, and guide teams through complex design trade-offs.
  • Stay hands-on by prototyping, writing critical-path code, and validating architecture in live systems.
  • Present investment and architecture proposals to senior leadership, mentor engineering leads, and scale technical expertise across the organization.

You're Our Person If...

  • You have 12+ years of experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems or infrastructure services, with a proven track record of driving multi-team technical strategy into production.
  • You have deep expertise in distributed-systems architecture, reliability, and performance at scale.
  • You have hands-on experience operating mission-critical, highly available services on public cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Kubernetes and service mesh.
  • You have security domain experience in identity and authorization, applied cryptography, or infrastructure security.
  • You have working knowledge of PKI, X.509 certificates, mutual Transport Layer Security (mTLS), and key management.
  • You have proven leadership in aligning cross-organizational initiatives without direct authority.
  • You have strong communication skills, with a track record of authoring adopted architecture proposals and presenting effectively to both engineers and executives.
  • You bring a demonstrated, genuine AI-first approach to engineering, using AI to move faster, build fluency across the stack, and contribute well beyond your core specialty.
  • You have experience using AI tools (for example, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor) in development workflows.
  • You hold a related technical degree.

Even Better If...

  • You have built or operated certificate, identity, or key-management services at scale.
  • You are familiar with workload identity standards (for example, Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone (SPIFFE)) and short-lived credentials.
  • You know post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards, such as Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM), Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA), and hybrid key exchange in TLS 1.3, as well as emerging approaches like Merkle Tree Certificates and crypto-agility design principles.

The REWS Workplace Innovation team is seeking a Workplace Research Manager to serve as the primary owner, operational driver, and analytical engine of our global Site Experience Survey Program. In this individual contributor role, you will bring analytical curiosity, proactive problem-solving, and quantitative rigor to our research, translating employee sentiment datasets into actionable findings that uncover the underlying drivers of workplace experience.

  • Reporting to the Senior Manager, Workplace Research, you will serve as a dedicated survey research partner and subject matter expert across Workplace Innovation teams (Pilots, Space Insights) and other REWS stakeholders.
  • In this role, you will own the global Site Experience Survey Program end-to-end, partnering closely with the Site Study Program Lead and Space Insights team to connect employee sentiment with spatial telemetry and observational data.

  • This role is based in San Francisco, CA, Chicago, IL, or Atlanta, GA, and is eligible for an Office Flexible (3 days/week) work arrangement, with potential for occasional domestic or international travel for site studies.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

  • Own and execute the global Site Experience Survey Program end-to-end, developing longitudinal benchmarking and driving continuous refinement of survey instruments. Bring proactive analytical curiosity to explore datasets—applying statistical techniques like correlation, regression, key driver analysis, and segmentation—to move beyond descriptive reporting, uncover non-obvious trends across multi-office datasets, and develop data-driven workplace personas.
  • Partner closely with the Site Study Program Lead and Space Insights team to bridge and integrate disparate data streams into strategic site study reports. Connect employee survey sentiment with objective spatial telemetry (such as occupancy patterns and room utilization metrics) to co-develop executive-ready recommendations that guide long-term workplace design, space allocations, and capital investment decisions.
  • Serve as a survey research and questionnaire design subject matter expert across REWS, advising internal teams and project leads on question design, rating scales, and practical sampling strategies across a diverse range of measurement scenarios (e.g., workplace pilot evaluations, guest experience, meeting and event feedback, and pre-design needs assessments).
  • Take hands-on ownership of day-to-day survey operations and data hygiene, configuring, maintaining, and refining templated survey instruments, coordinating with internal communications to manage distribution, and preparing clean datasets for analysis. Partner with the REWS Technology and Data Engineering (TEDI) team to evolve self-serve dashboards, while integrating AI tools to streamline qualitative text analytics.

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience designing, fielding, and analyzing quantitative surveys within corporate real estate, workplace strategy, environmental psychology, people analytics, or an applied organizational research setting.
  • Demonstrated analytical curiosity and practical quantitative skills (including significance testing, correlation, regression modeling, and key driver analysis) paired with solid survey design fundamentals (scale reliability, questionnaire design) to independently uncover actionable drivers from large, multi-office datasets.
  • Demonstrated experience configuring, updating, and managing survey instruments within enterprise platforms (such as SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics, or similar), alongside practical experience cleaning, transforming, and joining datasets (using SQL, Python/pandas, R/tidyverse, Tableau Prep, or similar data workflows) and hands-on proficiency with open-source statistical tools (specifically R or Python) to independently conduct exploratory and inferential analysis.

Slack is at an inflection point. We're evolving from the world's most beloved team communication tool into something fundamentally new: an AI operating system where humans and agents work together to get things done. Built on the context of your work, Slack becomes a single, personalized command center that replaces fragmented apps, inboxes, and point solutions.

As agents take on more of the work, the words between humans and machines carry more weight than ever. They set expectations, signal intent, earn trust, and keep people in control. Content design is a key part of what makes Slack feel like Slack. As the platform evolves, content designers as language experts will be at the center of defining these new experiences. We're looking for a leader with deep UX and content craft, that is excited about defining the evolution of work and the judgment to work through the hard tradeoffs AI brings. You'll grow a high-performing team of content designers, champion their work and careers, and make content design a core part of how Slack builds its future.

  • You look for growth opportunities for everyone on the team

  • Lead and grow a high-performing team of content designers who define how natural language, both written and spoken, shapes how people and agents work together in Slack. Champion your team's careers through performance, promotion, and growth conversations, and help them through people logistics like relocation and sabbaticals
  • Champion content design at the executive level, and own naming, terminology, and language decisions with product leadership. Partner with product design, product management, and engineering to make content design a core part of how Slack builds
  • Raise the bar on content craft and quality across AI-native experiences and traditional UI. Evolve team operations with the team, building on what works and creating clear paths for feedback to flow up

What You’ll Be Doing & Why It Matters

The Real Estate Strategy and Planning team shapes how Salesforce’s global office portfolio evolves. As Real Estate Strategy Senior Manager, you will be the finance lead behind our portfolio strategy and the key link between Real Estate, Finance and Transactions. You’ll turn real estate options into clear financial decisions by building scenario models, evaluating P&L impact and calculating return on investment. You’ll partner closely with Finance on long-range planning, budget, outlook and accounting impact, and with the Transactions team to turn the best scenarios into executed deals. Working with the VP of Real Estate Strategy and Planning and Finance, you’ll maintain a comprehensive long-range plan for the portfolio. Using AI tools and platforms, you’ll speed up modeling, analysis and reporting so leaders get answers faster.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Finance partnership: Serve as the main Real Estate partner to FP&A, Controllership and Accounting. Align on assumptions, budget and quarterly outlook, and make sure real estate impacts flow accurately into company plans and forecasts.
  • Transactions partnership: Work side by side with the Transactions team from scenario to signed deal. Model deal terms (rent, tenant improvement allowances, free rent, term, options), test proposals against the business case, and support negotiations with clear financial guidance.
  • Long-range planning: Partner with the VP of Real Estate Strategy and Planning and Finance to build and maintain a comprehensive long-range plan for the global portfolio, covering footprint, cost, capital and lease events. Keep it current as business plans change.
  • Scenario modeling: Build and own financial models for portfolio scenarios, including consolidations, expansions, exits, relocations, renewals vs. new deals, and footprint optimization.
  • Financial impact analysis: Quantify P&L, cash flow, capex/opex and balance sheet impact. Calculate ROI, NPV, IRR and payback to compare options and recommend a path.
  • Lease economics and accounting: Apply lease accounting knowledge, working with Accounting, so scenario outputs reflect the reported impact of decisions such as exits, renewals and early terminations.
  • Scorecard and metrics: Develop the REWS portfolio scorecard and metrics with Finance (cost per seat, cost per sq ft, utilization, occupancy, spend vs. plan). Monitor results and lead root cause analysis when metrics move.
  • Strategic initiatives: Lead the prioritization and delivery of high-visibility initiatives end to end, with full accountability for outcomes.
  • AI-enabled finance: Use AI tools and platforms to build and stress-test scenario models faster, automate recurring reporting and lease data analysis, and draft executive summaries and presentation materials. Find workflows that can be streamlined with AI or automation, and help the team adopt them.
  • Dashboards and interactive tools: Build dashboards and interactive scenario tools that let leaders explore financial tradeoffs and portfolio metrics on their own.
  • Executive communication: Write and edit complex analyses, decks and recommendations for senior leadership, and represent REWS with internal and external stakeholders.



Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in corporate finance, FP&A, real estate finance, investment banking or consulting
  • Expert financial modeling skills, including scenario and sensitivity analysis, DCF, ROI, NPV and IRR
  • Experience building and maintaining long-range plans or multi-year forecasts
  • Strong working knowledge of lease economics and lease accounting, and how real estate decisions flow through the P&L and balance sheet
  • Proven track record of partnering closely with Finance teams and deal or transaction teams to deliver results
  • Hands-on use of AI tools to speed up modeling, analysis and reporting, and to reduce manual work
  • Experience building business cases and recommendations for senior executives
  • Ability to lead cross-functional work and influence stakeholders across Finance, Accounting, Transactions and operating teams
  • Ability to think strategically while staying hands-on and detailed in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or related field



Preferred Qualifications

  • Corporate real estate experience, ideally with a multi-country or global office portfolio
  • Experience supporting real estate transactions, such as lease negotiations, renewals, exits or dispositions
  • Experience building KPI frameworks, dashboards and interactive tools in BI and AI platforms such as Tableau
  • Experience building AI-powered or automated finance workflows
  • MBA, CPA or CFA

The Real Estate and Workplace Services (REWS) organization designs, operates, and evolves the environments and experiences that enable Salesforce employees and customers to do their best work. Spanning more than 30 countries, our Agentic Campus reflects our values and culture – bringing together humans, agents, and robots to create inclusive, purpose-driven spaces where people feel a true sense of belonging. descriptionHtml:

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About the team


Assurance at Salesforce is being rebuilt as an engineering discipline. Legacy GRC runs on spreadsheets, screenshots, and an annual scramble to prove controls worked months ago. We're replacing it with a model that is continuous, automated, and built into how Salesforce ships. Controls are code. Evidence comes from pipelines, not people chasing tickets.

  • Risk-informed, control managed. We monitor, validate, and improve the controls that stand against threats and failures.
  • Visibility and invention. We give Salesforce a clear, current view of its security posture, and we invest in the people who build it.
  • Always in front. Nothing waits for the next audit to surface.

You'll have real ownership, a real roadmap, and the chance to define what modern assurance looks like for the industry.


What you'll be doing:


As a Sr. Security Governance Engineer, you'll translate enterprise security policies, regulatory requirements, and risk expectations into measurable, technically actionable controls. You'll help build a governance framework where policies and standards are version-controlled, validated, and integrated into engineering workflows. Over time, you'll grow into a Security Control Family Owner for domains such as IAM, Cloud, Application Security, Cryptography, Data Protection, or Infrastructure Security. The focus is governance, control design, and policy ownership. It is not hands-on software development.

  • Policy and standards: Develop and maintain security policies, technical standards, and control requirements. Manage the policy lifecycle: versioning, approvals, exceptions, reviews, and change management. Keep them aligned with architecture, risk appetite, and regulatory obligations.
  • Governance-as-Code / Policy-as-Code: Define structured, machine-readable policy and control requirements. Work with engineering to turn them into guardrails and validation criteria, using tools like OPA/Rego or cloud-native policy frameworks. You won't necessarily own the implementation. Review implementations for alignment with policy intent.
  • Control framework: Maintain a common control framework with clear objectives, ownership, and validation criteria. Establish traceability from regulation to policy to control to implementation. Set expectations for preventive, detective, and compensating controls, and support continuous evaluation of control effectiveness.
  • Control family ownership: Act as the SME and point of contact for your assigned domains. Interpret regulations, assess gaps, exceptions, and emerging risks, and recommend improvements.
  • Collaboration: Work with Security Engineering, Product Security, Cloud Security, IAM, Compliance, Risk, Audit, Legal, and business teams. Bring a governance perspective to architecture and design discussions.

Expected Outcomes

  • Decision speed: Rules are obvious, decisions are fast, and outputs are predictable, with governance built into the engineering workflow.
  • Scalable governance: Policies and control requirements are clear, consistent, and technically actionable.
  • Governance-as-Code adoption: Requirements are version-controlled, traceable, and integrated into security practices.
  • Alignment and visibility: Written policies, technical guardrails, and implemented controls match. Regulations, risks, controls, and evidence are clearly linked.
  • Control family SMEs: Dedicated owners set policy direction and technical standards for each domain.

What you should have:

  • U.S. Citizenship or Permanent Residency required — we're unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role.
  • 2+ years in information security governance, security engineering, technology risk, or related functions
  • Strong grasp of security policies, standards, control frameworks, and governance processes
  • Familiarity with NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or PCI DSS
  • Ability to turn regulatory and security requirements into measurable control objectives
  • Working knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, or GCP), IAM, application, infrastructure, and data security
  • Understanding of control design (preventive and detective), risk assessment, and exception management
  • Familiarity with modern development practices, cloud environments, and CI/CD
  • Strong analytical, communication, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Governance-as-Code or Policy-as-Code, and policy engines such as OPA/Rego or HashiCorp Sentinel
  • Familiarity with YAML, JSON, Git, infrastructure-as-code, and DevSecOps
  • Experience with GRC platforms, Common Controls Frameworks (CCF), and OSCAL
  • Exposure to security posture management, compliance validation, architecture reviews, or AI governance

How We Work:

  • Engineering-first. We use version control, code review, CI/CD, and backlogs. Assurance work ships like software.
  • Automate first. If it's done manually twice, it's a candidate for a build.
  • Signals, not surprises. Gaps become alerts and workflows, and control failures resolve through defined escalation paths.
  • Embedded partners. We work alongside T&P teams as peers, not gatekeepers, and solve problems with them, not at them.
  • Outcomes over activity. We measure risk reduced, effort saved, and audit friction removed.
  • Room to grow. Learn the engineering side if you come from GRC, or the risk side if you come from engineering. We support both paths.
