What You’ll Be Doing & Why It Matters

We are building the autonomous “software factory” that powers Slack’s global engineering organization.

As a Principal Member of Technical Staff (PMTS) / Staff Software Engineer on the Agentic Operations team, you will set the technical direction and architecture for how Slack builds, registers, and safely operates autonomous agentic systems. You will lead cross-team initiatives to transform high-volume software engineering workflows—from multi-repo code generation to automated incident remediation—into dependable, supervised, and continuously improving agentic pipelines at enterprise scale.

The Agentic Operations team builds and operates the platforms and internal “software factories” that automate how Slack’s engineering organization develops, operates, and maintains its services. Our mission is to turn repetitive, high-volume engineering toil into reliable, supervised autonomous workflows so engineers can focus on architecture and judgment.

We design and operate the systems that power:

  • Autonomous Code Generation & Remediation: Agent-driven pipelines that open, review, test, and land changes at scale across large codebases.
  • Operational & Incident Automation: Agents that assist with real-time incident response, post-incident remediation, and routine production maintenance.
  • Continuous Evaluation, Guardrails & Safety: Deterministic evaluation harnesses, regression test suites, and observability platforms that make non-deterministic agentic systems trustworthy in production.
  • Durable Execution & State Management: Robust execution engines featuring state persistence, function-calling hooks, human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gates, and automated rollback mechanisms.
  • Continuous Data Hygiene: Agentic loops that keep Slack’s service catalog and entity metadata current and verified.



Our systems build on Slack’s agentic development platform (Speck), our Compute Platform (EKS, EC2), and the Service catalog. We define the patterns, guardrails, and operational standards that engineering teams across Slack adopt to safely run their own autonomous agents.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Set Technical Strategy & Architecture: Architect Slack’s agentic operations platform, defining the standards for building, registering, and operating autonomous agents and software factories safely at scale.
  • Build End-to-End Autonomous Pipelines: Design autonomous pipelines (code generation, bug fixing, incident remediation) equipped with orchestration, tool integrations, and human-in-the-loop controls needed to run unattended but accountably.
  • Establish Production AI Rigor: Build evaluation suites, regression harnesses, guardrails, and observability frameworks that make non-deterministic agentic systems measurable, debuggable, and safe.
  • Define Ownership & Accountability Models: Establish how failures in autonomous systems are detected, attributed, and remediated, including on-call policies and operational guardrails.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Adoption: Partner with platform teams (Speck, Incident Management, Deploy Safety) and consuming engineering groups to integrate agentic workflows into daily developer routines.
  • Cost & Compute Governance: Advocate for cost-conscious, efficient model and compute utilization, balancing model intelligence and latency against token budgets and compute spend.
  • Raise the Engineering Bar: Mentor senior engineers, drive deep architectural reviews, and author clear system designs that establish reusable technical patterns across the organization.



Minimum Requirements

  • 10+ Years of Software Engineering Experience: Proven track record designing and delivering complex distributed systems at scale, with Staff/Principal-level technical judgment and organizational influence.
  • Production Agentic Systems Experience: Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM-powered agents and multi-agent systems, including orchestration, structured tool/function calling, retrieval (RAG), and context window engineering.
  • Production AI Rigor & Evals: Concrete experience making non-deterministic AI systems production-ready through deterministic evaluation suites, regression harnesses, guardrails, and LLM telemetry.
  • Strong Distributed Systems & Backend Foundations: High engineering rigor in writing clean, scalable, maintainable code. Experience operating backend and distributed systems with direct accountability for uptime, latency, and reliability.
  • Systems-Level Automation Mindset: Pragmatic approach to developer platforms and automation, comfortable operating with ambiguity and balancing rapid AI capability against production safety.
  • Experience building autonomous code-generation pipelines, automated refactoring systems, or “software factories” that open PRs and land changes across monolithic or multi-repo architectures.
  • Experience designing agent evaluation frameworks, prompt/context management layers, or LLM observability platforms used by other engineering teams.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep background in service orchestration, or automated incident remediation at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS, Kubernetes (EKS), and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) using reusable, maintainable abstractions.
  • Active contributions to open-source agentic frameworks, developer tools, or the broader AI developer ecosystem.

Employment Type: Full-Time

About the Role

As a Technical Architect for the Slack Practice within Salesforce Professional Services (GDC), you will be the hands-on technical authority for complex Slack transformations. These range from large-scale Enterprise Grid migrations and custom app development to next-generation Agentforce and Salesforce integrations.

You will partner closely with global practice leaders, onshore engagement managers, and enterprise customers. You will design, lead, and deliver architectures that solve critical business challenges. This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities. It is 50% billable.

  • Serve as the lead Technical Architect for Slack enterprise implementations, providing architectural oversight across client deliverables.
  • Design and own solution architectures for Enterprise Grid, custom apps, integrations, and Slack + Salesforce use cases.
  • Establish best practices, reusable code repositories, standard operating frameworks, and review gates for Slack custom apps (Bolt framework, Block Kit, API limits, security).
  • Oversee enterprise migration architectures, covering identity mapping, data retention, DLP compliance, and cutover execution.
  • Champion architecture reviews and guide delivery teams through complex customer design challenges.
  • Lead functional and technical workshops, and demonstrate leadership in designing, building, testing, and deploying solutions.
  • Collaborate with onshore delivery teams to scope technical effort, review estimates, and ensure seamless global delivery.

  • Mentor and coach consultants and developers on technical topics, and contribute to certification bootcamps (Certified Slack Developer, Certified Slack Admin) and enablement on emerging features (Agentforce in Slack, Slack CLI).
  • Support technical interviews to help scale the practice.
  • Work with Resource Management and Practice Directors on project readiness and technical staffing needs.

Required Technical Skills & Competencies

Slack Enterprise Grid & Administration

  • Deep understanding of Enterprise Grid topology, multi-workspace scoping, and enterprise governance.
  • Experience with identity lifecycle management: SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Azure AD, Ping) and SCIM directory sync.
  • Strong foundation in enterprise security, compliance, DLP, eDiscovery, EKM, and the Slack Audit Logs API.
  • Governance of Slack Connect, external collaboration policies, and app installation approval pipelines.



Slack App Development & APIs

  • Proven hands-on experience with the Bolt Framework (Node.js or Python).
  • Mastery of Block Kit, interactive components, modals, and App Home architectures.
  • Thorough knowledge of the Web API, Events API, Webhooks, Socket Mode vs. HTTP endpoints, and rate-limiting best practices.
  • Familiarity with the Slack CLI, modular app architecture, manifest.json, and Workflow Builder custom functions.



Enterprise Migration & Consolidation

  • Architectural knowledge of migrating from Microsoft Teams, Mattermost, and freemium or standalone Slack workspaces to Enterprise Grid.
  • Familiarity with user/channel mapping schemas, export/import APIs, data parity verification, and cutover runbooks.



DevOps & Engineering Standards

  • Solid understanding of CI/CD pipelines, Git workflows, automated testing, and secure API integration standards.
  • Experience hosting Slack apps on Heroku, AWS, GCP, or Azure.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Total Experience: 10-15+ years in software engineering, technical consulting, or enterprise cloud solutions.
  • Architecture Experience: 5+ years as a technical architect or lead designing and delivering enterprise solutions in a global delivery or consulting model.
  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

About Salesforce

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

What is a Solution Engineer?
Also known as a " Pre -Sales Engineer" or "Sales Consultant," the Solution Engineer is responsible for presenting product offerings and architecture in the best light to prospects and customers, to evoke confidence in the company's technology infrastructure, and to remove all technical objections in the sales cycle. To accomplish this, the Solution Engineer must have a strong desire to leverage their technical and/or sales skills, including the ability to solicit business requirements, develop a technical sales strategy, configure and effectively demonstrate the solutions that address these requirements and provide business value.

Lead, Specialist Solution Engineer
Are you a seasoned analytics expert who loves turning complex data challenges into clear, compelling solutions? As a Lead Solution Engineer, Analytics at Salesforce, you'll go beyond traditional pre-sales: you'll lead the technical strategy on your most strategic opportunities and help customers build a trusted, governed semantic foundation for their analytics. You'll be a recognized technical authority on Tableau's semantic layer and analytics interoperability, and a trusted advisor to business and technical stakeholders across LATAM.

What You'll Be Doing
The Lead Specialist Solution Engineer leads the technical sales cycle for Analytics on complex opportunities, from vision co-creation through storytelling demos to deep-dive workshops, showing customers the "why" and the "what." You'll run deep discovery on business and data needs, then design and demo semantic models that define metrics, dimensions, and business rules once and make them reusable and governed across the organization. You'll position Tableau Semantics and Tableau Next alongside Tableau Cloud and Server, and show how analytics interoperability and Tableau Knowledge help customers unify their data context across platforms. You'll partner with Account Executives to recommend solutions with measurable ROI, and share best practices with peers through demos and discovery coaching. Ideal candidates have experience with Tableau, CRM Analytics, the Salesforce core platform, Data 360 / data integration, semantic modeling, and BI in a customer-facing role.

Your Impact

  • Build trusted advisor relationships with business and technical stakeholders by:
    • Understanding their business challenges and data/analytics strategy
    • Identifying the best Tableau solution for their needs
    • Supporting them in achieving their business goals
  • Help customers become more data-driven by showcasing Tableau and building excitement around the platform
  • Lead discovery sessions and workshops with business users to define, build, and implement solution prototypes
  • Design and demo semantic models (Tableau Semantics, Published Data Sources) that define metrics and business rules once, with governance, for reuse across the organization
  • Build and present customized demos that prove business value, including analytics interoperability across Tableau Cloud, Server, Tableau Next, and CRM Analytics
  • Position recent Tableau innovations (Tableau Next, Tableau Semantics, Tableau Knowledge) and explain how they fit with the customer's existing data stack
  • Articulate the business value of Tableau to managers and business leaders
  • Deliver technical responses on RFPs/RFIs
  • Support adjacent teams in positioning Tableau and Salesforce's analytics portfolio
  • Handle multiple customer engagements at once across LATAM, prioritizing with the sales team
  • Share customer feedback with the product GTM team and contribute to analytics thought leadership across LATAM
  • Share best practices with peers through demos and knowledge sharing



What we're looking for

We're seeking a proactive professional with solid presales or technical expertise gained in the software/IT industry or as an end user. Ideally, you bring broad technical knowledge plus specialized expertise in one or more of these areas: data visualization/analytics, BI, semantic modeling, data quality, integration, databases, or analytics infrastructure.

  • Experienced: Proven ability to build trust with customers and navigate the sales cycle, with 3+ years in technical pre-sales or consulting and a B.S. in Computer Science, Software Engineering, MIS or equivalent
  • Technically strong: Hands-on experience in one or more of the areas above. Python and/or JavaScript is a plus. Experience analyzing data, identifying trends, and building visualizations
  • Specialized knowledge: Experience building and delivering PoCs and answering the technical and functional parts of RFIs/RFPs. Familiarity with Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar tools. Experience with data modeling, semantic layers, star schema design, and data warehouse concepts
  • Passionate: Solid expertise in analytics and data strategy, with the ability to help shape customer vision and turn it into business impact
  • Strong communicator: Excellent verbal and written communication, and the ability to present to diverse audiences
  • Languages: English and Spanish required. Portuguese is a plus
  • Sales-minded: Able to support the sales team with objection handling, business value articulation, and product positioning

We are looking for a senior strategic finance leader with experience as a startup financial operator to validate and operationalize the financial deal model during due diligence, and build and own the operating models supporting AI Labs acquisitions and strategic investments, taking ownership of financial budgets to ensure post-close success.


This role will ensure that financial models reflect how AI-native companies actually operate and that the commitments made before close translate into executable post-close plans.

What You'll Actually Be Doing


  • Own the end-to-end operating models for AI Labs acquisitions.
  • Validate assumptions across revenue, growth, headcount, compensation, investment, margin, and cash requirements with both AI Labs leadership and founding teams
  • After close, partner directly with portfolio CEOs/founders and AI Labs leadership to align on assumptions of existing budget and growth metrics established and before further investment decisions are made.

  • Operationalize approved acquisition and strategic investment models into executable post-close budgets and operating plans to drive growth and innovation.
  • Track actual performance against financial model assumptions and create processes that identify material variances early, feedback loop, resolution paths to get business back on track.. 
  • Operate and own a forward looking driver based revenue forecast to ensure deal model assumptions can be achieved. 
  • Establish a consistent modeling framework across AI Labs acquisitions that also incorporates differences in company stage and business model.

You're Our Person If...


  • Experience as a CFO, strategic finance leader, or senior finance executive in a Series B–D or similarly high-growth technology company.
  • Deep understanding of startup economics, SaaS/AI business models, and growth-stage operating decisions.
  • Exceptional financial modeling skills and analytical judgment.
  • Experience partnering directly with founders and executive teams,Comfortable challenging assumptions and bringing an operator's perspective to investment decisions.
  • Problem solver mindset to unlock barriers to growth by working with AI Lab companies and Salesforce’s larger ecosystem.

  • Experience conducting benchmark and/or work-load testing using automation tools and frameworks for performance measurement and analysis (Jmeter)

What You'll Be Doing & Why It Matters

MuleSoft Security Engineering protects the Anypoint Platform and the infrastructure it runs on. As a Senior Security Engineer focused on infrastructure, you will design, build, and operate identity, network, and cloud security controls in AWS.

You will work in a FedRAMP environment and meet its security control requirements. Federal regulations restrict access to this environment to U.S. citizens working from the U.S.

Core Responsibilities & Scope

  • Implement and maintain security controls that satisfy FedRAMP requirements, mapped to NIST SP 800-53.
  • Engineer secure network architecture in AWS: VPC design, segmentation, security groups, NACLs, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, WAF, and egress controls.
  • Design and improve identity and access management: IdP integration, SSO, federation (SAML, OIDC, OAuth), IAM roles and policies, least privilege, privileged access, secrets management, and KMS key management.
  • Build and maintain infrastructure as code in Terraform, including reusable modules, secure defaults, policy-as-code, and automated guardrails.
  • Harden and secure Linux systems and containers, including host baselines, runtime security, and Kubernetes workloads.
  • Support continuous monitoring: vulnerability remediation within required timelines, POA&M tracking, and evidence collection for audits.
  • Automate control validation and evidence gathering.
  • Partner with Engineering, SRE, and Compliance to embed security into the SDLC and deployment pipelines.
  • Contribute to incident response and detection engineering, including logging, SIEM integration, and alerting.
  • Produce clear technical documentation and architecture reviews, and mentor other engineers.



Minimum Requirements

  • 5+ years in security engineering, cloud security, or infrastructure security.
  • Experience implementing and meeting security controls in a FedRAMP environment, or an equivalent framework (for example, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, or CMMC).
  • Solid knowledge of NIST security controls, including control families, baselines, and how to map them to technical implementations.
  • Strong, hands-on Terraform skills, including module design, state management, and CI/CD-driven deployments.
  • Deep experience with network security engineering in AWS (VPC, Transit Gateway, security groups, WAF, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, CloudTrail).
  • Hands-on identity engineering: IdPs, SAML, OIDC, OAuth 2.0, and directory and authentication protocols (LDAP, Kerberos), plus AWS IAM and KMS.
  • Strong understanding of TLS and PKI, including certificate lifecycle management and secure protocol configuration.
  • Strong Linux systems and container experience.
  • Proficiency in a scripting language (Python, Go, or Bash).
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including working with auditors and engineering teams.
  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to work from the U.S., as required by federal regulation for access to the FedRAMP environment. Willingness to complete additional screening or background checks as required.



Preferred Qualifications

  • Practical experience using AI tools to accelerate engineering work, with sound judgment in reviewing AI-generated code and configurations for security.
  • Experience supporting a FedRAMP authorization, annual assessment, or 3PAO assessment.
  • Experience with Kubernetes security at scale.
  • Working knowledge of vulnerability management, patching, and remediation workflows.
  • Familiarity with FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptography.
  • Experience with AWS GovCloud.
  • Experience with FedRAMP 20x, continuous monitoring automation, OSCAL and/or similar frameworks and technologies.
  • Familiarity with CISA directives and DISA STIGs.
  • Experience with policy-as-code (OPA, Sentinel, Checkov) and software supply chain security.
  • Certifications such as AWS Security Specialty, CKS, CCSP or similar is preferred.



What Success Looks Like

  • First 90 days: You understand the infrastructure architecture and control inventory, and you own remediation of a defined set of control gaps.
  • 6 months: You deliver network and identity security improvements through Terraform and automate at least one control validation workflow.
  • 12 months: You are a recognized technical authority for AWS infrastructure security and compliance, and you help keep the team audit-ready.

We are looking for a Principal Compliance Engineer who can take a FedRAMP or DoD requirement and determine whether the system meets it. You review the architecture and the running implementation for government cloud services and for on-prem products: network design, access, cryptography, containers, data stores, and the pipeline that builds them. You are part of the engineering team and evaluate the system changes before they happen.

You evaluate government-cloud and on-prem environments against FedRAMP, DoD, FIPS 140-3, STIG, and CIS requirements. You identify gaps in the running system and in the build, determine the remediation, and drive that remediation through implementation until the control is met. This includes live clusters and product configuration, FIPS validation in the pipeline and the image, and vulnerabilities in the versions that are deployed.

You cover both cloud and on-premises deployment models. Government cloud work is FedRAMP Rev 5 and DoD IL5: what the platform inherits, what the service implements, and whether a change is significant. On-prem work covers the stack the customer runs, including the operating system, Kubernetes, the container runtime, databases, and the application. You provide secure-configuration recommendations, support customer authority-to-operate efforts, conduct CVE reviews, determine compensating controls where a requirement cannot be met directly, and manage end-of-life monitoring.

What You'll Actually Be Doing:

  • Review architectural designs for new products, system changes, and FedRAMP onboarding for security and compliance impact. This includes network security, boundary protection, ingress and egress, identity and access, privileged access, service accounts, tenant isolation, encryption in transit and at rest, key management and PKI, audit logging, session management, backup and recovery, and privacy and PII handling.
  • Apply FedRAMP Rev 5 and DoD IL5 as engineering requirements. Decide what is inherited, what is shared, what the product must implement, and what remains the customer's responsibility. Support significant-change packages, System Security Plan updates, and control narratives that cite the implementation.
  • Evaluate STIG and CIS controls for operating systems, Kubernetes, container platforms, and databases. Review scanner findings, determine false positives, identify compensating controls, and identify gaps in scan coverage. Write the finding, the evidence, and the recommended remediation..
  • Evaluate FIPS 140-2/3 adherence in the build and at runtime. Including approved module and provider selection, TLS configuration, and detection of non-approved algorithms and providers in product code, connectors, and base images.
  • Follow the control into the engineering system. Evaluate Dockerfiles, Helm charts, Kubernetes manifests, CI logs, and service configuration. Use CI/CD and static analysis, including Semgrep, to turn compliance checks into repeatable pipeline gates. Decide when a finding is a real deviation and when the pipeline or the control interpretation is wrong.
  • Own vulnerability evidence for authorized systems. Triage KEV and critical CVEs against the deployed artifact and version, trace reachability through images and code, and produce customer-ready technical responses and POA&M-quality records.
  • Maintain authorization systems of record: baseline configuration, component and image inventory, end-of-life platforms, SSP updates, and continuous-monitoring evidence.
  • Advise product and platform engineers in design reviews. Translate a failed control into a specific code, config, or architecture change, and push back when a proposed fix does not satisfy the requirement.
  • Represent the implementation to a 3PAO and to customers. Support customer calls and evaluate support cases that involve the compliance or security of the system.



You're Our Person If:


  • 5 or more years in software engineering, infrastructure, security, or compliance; building or auditing production systems.
  • Expert working knowledge of FedRAMP Rev 5, including High and Moderate, control inheritance, significant change, the System Security Plan, POA&M, and continuous monitoring. You can write a control implementation description from the system, not from a template.
  • Expert working knowledge of DoD cloud authorization at IL4/IL5, including the Cloud Computing SRG and DISA STIGs. You have evaluated controls against check text and fix text and can tell a scanner false positive from a real finding.
  • Demonstrated STIG or CIS evaluation of infrastructure. At least two of: Kubernetes, a Linux STIG (RHEL or equivalent), container runtime or Docker CIS, and a database STIG (PostgreSQL or equivalent).
  • Strong working knowledge of FIPS 140-2 and FIPS 140-3. Experience evaluating FIPS 140 compliance in programming languages and system configurations, including cryptographic providers, approved algorithms, and TLS settings in application code, connectors, and container images.
  • Practical fluency with Kubernetes, containers, Helm or equivalent packaging, Linux, network security, and identity. You are comfortable in a repo, a Dockerfile, and a CI log.
  • Strong understanding of vulnerability management and continuous monitoring. Experience evaluating CVEs for system impact, compensating controls, risk acceptance, and remediation recommendations.
  • Python or equivalent scripting around scanners, inventories, and evidence pipelines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication; comfortable influencing without direct authority


Even Better If:

  • Experience taking a product onto FedRAMP High or DoD IL5 through a significant change or a new authorization, including 3PAO evidence packages.
  • OSCAL, SSP automation, or control-inheritance mapping across a platform and a product.
  • Privacy overlays used by federal customers: NIST SP 800-122, and working familiarity with CJIS or IRS Publication 1075 where the system handles that data.
  • Supply-chain and base-image work: distro end of life, image lineage, and rebuild strategy for government environments.
  • Direct technical work with defense or civilian customers on STIG deviations, CVE responses, or architecture questions.

Our mission is to incubate, scale, and grow these solutions with a startup mindset. As a Specialist Solution Engineer, you will be instrumental in demonstrating and evangelizing two critical solution areas:

  • Salesforce Partner Ecosystem Management (PEM): The Hub for Partner Success
    Our PEM solution provides a unified, scalable platform for businesses to manage their entire partner lifecycle. This comprehensive "partner command center" eliminates fragmented systems and administrative complexity. You'll be selling a solution that helps companies:Streamline Partner Onboarding & Engagement: Simplify the entire process from recruitment to ongoing collaboration, ensuring partners are quickly enabled and integrated.Boost Partner Productivity: Provide secure, customizable partner portals, automation tools, and integrated access to sales processes (leads, opportunities, quotes, orders) for more efficient partner work.Enhance Partner Enablement: Deliver targeted training, marketing content, and essential resources to ensure partners have what they need to succeed.Optimize Channel Strategy: Leverage rich insights and analytics to guide partner tiering, incentive programs, and overall business planning, enabling data-driven decisions.Facilitate Seamless Collaboration: Foster real-time collaboration between internal teams and partners, ensuring coordinated support and faster deal velocity.
  • Salesforce Channel Revenue Solutions: Maximizing Channel Profitability
    Complementing PEM, our Channel Revenue Solutions are designed to optimize and automate the complex financial aspects of channel sales, including the powerful Revenue Cloud and specialized Channel Revenue Management capabilities. You'll be helping clients:Automate Product-to-Cash Processes: Enable end-to-end revenue generation and management on a single, trusted platform, supporting both one-time sales and subscription services.Simplify Pricing & Quoting: Streamline product catalog management, define consistent pricing models, and empower sales reps (both direct and and partner) to configure complex products and generate accurate quotes with ease.Optimize Rebate and Incentive Programs: Gain total control over program setup, track and enforce all types of rebate programs (growth, volume, ship and debit, price protection), and ensure accurate payouts, building partner trust and loyalty.Gain Unified Visibility: Bring all channel inventory, rebates, payouts, and transaction data into Salesforce, providing a complete picture of partner activity and financial performance.Drive Channel Growth: Motivate partners through automated deal registration, streamlined claim submissions, and transparent insights into new opportunities and payout statuses, directly impacting their bottom line and your client's revenue.



A Specialist Solution Engineer plays a pivotal role in aligning innovative strategies to technology solutions within complex accounts. This role focuses on partnering with clients and collaborating with internal team members and C-level client contacts to drive consensus on multi-product technology solutions across the various Salesforce product lines.

  • Attend events to evangelize solutions (Salesforce World Tours, industry events, Dreamforce).
  • Internally evangelize the solutions across our Core and Service Cloud Account Executives (AEs) and Solution Engineers (SEs).
  • Stay up to date on product innovation to be able to speak to and demonstrate key features and benefits.

  • Solid oral, written, presentation, collaboration, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to work as part of a team to solve technical problems in varied environments.
  • Strong presentation skills, both virtually and in person.
  • Value proposition-minded with strong business acumen.



Even Better If...

  • Preferred experience with Sales Cloud, Experience Cloud, and/or Marketing Cloud.
  • Salesforce Admin 201 certification or similar technical certification preferred.
  • Previous experience as a solution/sales engineer for a CRM company or similar technology.
  • Fluency in English and French, or German.

The Experience


The Digital Enterprise Technology (DET) Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) team drives how Salesforce scales through aligned investment decisions, trusted portfolio data, and an integrated tooling ecosystem. We're transforming from fragmented portfolio management practices to a unified, data-driven operating model — building the systems, processes, governance, and insights that enable DET leaders to prioritize strategically, plan effectively, and deliver with confidence. Our FY28 strategy is anchored on five inter-connected domains: Portfolio Planning, Data & Systems Optimization, Tooling Enablement, Process Excellence & Governance, and Capacity Planning.


We are seeking a Strategic Portfolio Operations, Senior Analyst — a frontline, service-oriented role sitting at the intersection of Tooling Enablement and Portfolio Planning. You'll be a go-to resource for portfolio tooling and support, a key contributor to the broader SPM tooling ecosystem, and a hands-on Portfolio Partner supporting assigned DET pillars through the planning process. This is a high-visibility position — you'll partner closely with Pillar Portfolio Managers (PPMs), senior analysts, tooling owners, and pillar stakeholders across DET, with real room for growth within portfolio management, program management, or business operations.


What You’ll Actually Be Doing


SPM Tooling Support & Project Management 


  • Provide frontline customer support for the SPM custom tool stack (Airtable, Time tracking, Google App Script), answering how-to questions, troubleshooting issues, and routing complex issues to system owners.
  • Apply project/program management discipline to SPM tooling and process initiatives — scoping enhancement requests, sequencing rollout plans, and tracking tooling projects from kickoff through delivery.
  • Manage and prioritize the SPM tooling support backlog, keeping requests organized and stakeholders informed.
  • Support maintenance of user documentation, FAQs, training materials, and process guides that drive adoption and consistency.
  • Identify recurring issues and surface opportunities to streamline workflows and improve the day-to-day tooling experience, escalating to tooling owners as needed.

Portfolio Partnership & Planning Support


  • Act as a Portfolio Partner for assigned DET pillars, assisting with Initiative intake, prioritization, and the quarterly/annual portfolio planning process.
  • Support pillar teams through planning activities — ensuring data is complete, accurate, and submitted on time — and coordinate deadlines, follow-ups, and deliverables across assigned pillars during planning cycles.
  • Help maintain portfolio data used for planning, reporting, and operational reviews.
  • Provide operational and reporting support to PPMs and pillar stakeholders, and help document portfolio operating procedures and planning process guides.

The Senior Builder Experience

  • Technical Ownership: Partner with a Deployment Strategist to own customer outcomes end-to-end. You're the senior technical authority in the room, ensuring deliverables meet the  highest engineering  standards, whether it was generated by an AI tool by a colleague or written by you directly. 
  • AI-Supported  Engineering: Cursor, Claude, and Salesforce coding products like Vibes are embedded in your  daily workflow. The conventions and patterns you develop tend to propagate through the team because other Builders look to your work as reference.
  • Roadmap Influence: Your field experience routes directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps you hit and the edge cases you encounter in real life customer environments become the features they ship. Senior Forward Deployed Engineers are the most credible voice in agentic AIproduct evolution.

What You'll Actually Be Building

  • Own end-to-end build and deployment of agentic AI solutions for Salesforce's most strategic customers — from architecture decisions through production handoff.
  • Design and ship agentic systems on the Agentforce platform: agent logic, tool calls, multi-agent orchestration, deterministic guardrails, and the integration patterns that hold up in enterprise environments. Your reference implementations become the basis for how other Builders approach similar problems.
  • Own the data lifecycle: model design, processing pipelines, and data readiness for AI applications across Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer-specific platforms.
  • Resolve the technical blockers that other engineers can't — data integration failures, model deployment issues, orchestration breakdowns, performance regressions. These problems are routed to you because of your track record of solving them.
  • Build and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer KPI reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes across engagements.
  • Develop proofs-of-concept and MVPs quickly, with the judgment to know which decisions can be deferred and which need to be right the first time.
  • Codify what you learn. The patterns, reusable assets, and internal frameworks that come out of your real customer work become the playbooks the rest of the org draws from.
  • Mentor other Engineers through code reviews, pair sessions, and shared work. Most of your influence on developing engineers happens inside the same codebases you're building in.
  • Provide technical depth on at-risk or strategically critical deployments when senior engineering judgment is needed.
  • Surface field insights directly to Product and Engineering. The gaps and edge cases you encounter in real customer environments are some of the most valuable inputs to the Agentforce roadmap.
  • Partner with the Deployment Strategist on your team to translate complex customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.

  • You have 6+ years of software engineering or technical delivery experience, with proven end-to-end ownership of scalable production systems in enterprise AI, cloud, or SaaS environments.
  • You have a degree in Computer Science or a related field
  • You're an expert in at least one of Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or Apex, and conversant in the others.
  • You've integrated LLMs into production, used frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex, and applied prompt engineering and responsible AI practices in real customer contexts.
  • You have deep experience in data modeling, processing, and analytics, with demonstrable proficiency across platforms like Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, or Databricks.
  • You bring deep Salesforce platform expertise: Agentforce, Apex, LWC, Flows, and Salesforce APIs.

  • You've mentored technical talent and created reusable assets — frameworks, playbooks, internal tooling.
  • You communicate clearly and credibly with engineering peers, customer architects, and executive stakeholders.
  • You actively tinker with the evolving AI/data landscape — piloting new tools, experimenting with new models, and staying genuinely curious about what's coming next.
  • You're excited to travel ~25% of the time, embedded with customer engineers.

You will work on the agent-based systems that take action on production infrastructure, including incident workflows and safe, validated rollback. Reliability, safety, and auditability matter as much as features.

We are hiring a Go-to-Market (GTM) Solutions Lead for Loyalty within the Salesforce Professional Services Global Acceleration Hub, supporting GTM execution across all regions.


As a GTM Solutions Lead you will apply deep domain, implementation, and technical expertise to shape services opportunities that drive NNAOV growth, position customers for success, and enable project teams to deliver lasting business outcomes through Salesforce solutions. We’re looking for a self-starter who leads with confidence and earns trust through credibility and results.
The role scales expertise through curated GTM assets, AI-enabled tooling, and field enablement, partnering flexibly with OU and cross-OU teams to help the broader seller ecosystem position and scope our offerings effectively. Through a variable engagement model, you’ll provide specialized guidance on products, solutions, offerings, and outcomes for large, complex, or emerging-technology pursuits.


As part of the Hub’s product-to-field engine, you’ll translate deal and market signals into actionable product feedback, keep the field current on new capabilities, and help refine and validate AI-enabled scoping tools and outputs that support AI-native delivery. Engagement risk patterns identified along the way feed back into shared assets, accelerators, and best practices.
Beyond pursuits, the role contributes to the broader Global Acceleration Hub Community through thought leadership and participation in strategic priorities and initiatives.


Core Responsibilities & ScopeResponsibilities

  • GTM Strategy & Leadership: Partner with OU and cross-OU Teams and Builder Orgs to calibrate the pre-sales engagement model for each product and region, defining where the Hub leads, where it supports, and where OUs self-serve.
  • Strategic Pursuit Support: Through a variable engagement model, provide specialized solution, scoping, offering, and outcome guidance for large, complex, or emerging-technology pursuits. Support discovery and contribute product and implementation expertise throughout the sales cycle, including advising on delivery skill requirements. Partner with Product Architect Leads, SSSLs, and Account Teams on solution design, scope validation, and effective pursuit-to-delivery hand-offs.
  • Deal Quality & Readiness: Help shape proposed work that is accurately scoped, deliverable, and aligned to customer business outcomes. Identify the business impact and value of proposed solutions, objectively assess customer readiness, and flag delivery and adoption risk. Uphold global scoping, estimating, and risk governance standards, and reflect them in field assets.
  • AI-Powered Enablement & Knowledge Management: Use AI tools and Salesforce platforms to curate and maintain an evolving library of GTM content: offerings, value accelerators, scoping templates, best practice assets, Services plays, and structured learning paths. Codify field insights and pursuit patterns into continuously refreshed, centrally accessible knowledge. Drive adoption through targeted enablement so sellers can self-serve.
  • AI-Enabled GTM Innovation: Curate and refine AI GTM tools and assets (e.g., modernized scoping tools, prompt libraries, and sizing and scoping accelerators), and validate their outputs to improve pre-sales efficiency and proposal quality. Apply these tools in active pursuits and measure their impact on speed and quality. Ensure evolving assets integrate with Global IT tooling (e.g., ADOS) and methodologies to support AI-native delivery.
  • Release Readiness: Act as an early adopter of new product innovation and releases, translating them into updated positioning, scoping guidance, and offering alignment ahead of general availability. Facilitate readiness enablement for pre-sales counterparts.
  • Product Relationship & Roadmap Influence: Build a trusted relationship with Product and Engineering Teams, in partnership with Product Architect Leads, serving as a primary Professional Services voice from the GTM side. Synthesize customer feedback, Voice of Service insights, and deal and market signals (e.g., win/loss patterns, scoping friction, competitive and pricing feedback) into concrete product input that shapes the roadmap.
  • Portfolio Health & Risk Prevention: Monitor the health of the product GTM portfolio across regions to detect demand patterns & signals before they become escalation trends, and partner with OU delivery leaders & Product Architect Leads to proactively help fill gaps in upcoming delivery skills/needs.
  • Customer Engagement & Delivery: Engage directly with customers on strategic or complex projects as a product subject matter expert, in line with the role’s utilization target. Channel pursuit and project insights back into the Hub and Community.
  • Customer Success Alignment: Partner with Customer Success Teams on adoption risks, expansion opportunities, and hand-offs to reduce attrition and support NNAOV growth.
  • Community & Thought Leadership: Champion the Global Acceleration Hub Community through knowledge sharing, peer engagement, and thought leadership. Proactively identify risk across Professional Services engagements and feed those lessons back into shared assets and feedback channels.
  • Measure Impact: Define and track KPIs that show the reach and impact of GTM initiatives across pursuits, delivery, and the field.

Minimum Requirements
 7+ years of relevant experience, including:
GTM & Delivery

  • Experience supporting Professional Services go-to-market in a pre-sales or delivery role.
  • Strong understanding of how services fit into the sales cycle, including discovery, scoping, and estimation on complex pursuits.
  • Consulting skills to translate customer goals and complex technical capabilities into business solutions, outcomes, and ROI.
  • Turns deep domain knowledge into industry standards and best practices for use across Professional Services.
  • Ability to assess pursuit needs and adapt engagement accordingly (providing strategic direction, leading efforts when needed, or enabling OU Teams to deliver) while balancing big-picture perspective with hands-on execution.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities across pursuit and client engagements while actively contributing to Global Acceleration Hub initiatives and strategic priorities.

Technical & Product

  • Demonstrated implementation or pre-sales experience with Salesforce and advanced [Product] capabilities.
  • [Product] certifications preferred.
  • Strong understanding of AI adoption, AI-native delivery approaches, and AI-enabled tooling, with practical experience applying these capabilities in pre-sales or delivery contexts, including assessing and validating AI-generated outputs.

Leadership & Interpersonal

  • Executive presence and communication: Exceptional communication and presentation skills; influences and engages customer leadership with authority, clarity, and confidence.
  • Facilitation and storytelling: Leads solutioning sessions, roadmapping workshops, and enterprise transformation discussions; confidently defends a point of view and lands clear, memorable messages.

Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.
